title: FCA proposes greater pension investment flexibility to support long-term value for savers
summary: Workplace pension providers could have greater flexibility to invest for the long term under proposals from the FCA, helping them deliver better outcomes for savers while ensuring savers' interests remain protected. The FCA is consulting on excluding certain performance-linked fees from the charge cap for default funds in workplace pensions it regulates.Performance-linked fees are common in private markets, including private equity, venture capital and private credit. The proposed change would give providers greater flexibility to access a broader range of investments where this could help improve long-term returns and value for savers.The FCA is clear that greater flexibility is not a licence to charge more. Providers should carefully weigh potential returns, risks and costs when making investment decisions, and any higher charges should be justified by the additional value delivered to savers.Alongside the proposed flexibility, the FCA is proposing safeguards covering transparency, fair allocation of fees between savers and scrutiny of how private assets are valued. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). summary: The German financial system is resilient, but operating in an environment of geopolitical tension. Increased risks arise from high valuations in the financial markets, rising credit risk, real estate financing vulnerabilities, high government debt and the growing importance of private credit. In addition, artificial intelligence and hybrid threats increase the risk of cyber attacks on critical financial services.

title: Ethiopia's accession maintains momentum as WTO members review progress
summary: At its eighth meeting on 9 and 10 November, the Working Party on Ethiopia's Accession to the WTO took stock of the latest progress in bilateral market access negotiations and reforms of Ethiopia's foreign trade regime. Leading a high-level delegation, Ethiopia's Minister of Trade and Regional Integration and Chief Trade Negotiator, Yasmin Wohabrebbi Saeed, reaffirmed the priority the government continues to attach to achieving WTO accession as soon as possible. Members welcomed the progress achieved while noting that further work is needed before the accession process can be concluded.
